prize_parts.citation: for transparent empirical evidence on how import competition reshapes local labour markets, employment and the distribution of earnings

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged in ballot and names: one part, B044, credited to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The citation is narrower than it was in round 1 and is anchored only on the trade-shock and local-labour-market evidence. That is the one strand where credit is a joint product of exactly these three people, and where I think the discovery is prize-sized by itself. Before the China-shock papers, the profession had no well-identified answer to who bears the cost of trade integration and how long adjustment takes. The design uses local labour markets, exposure measures and long-horizon outcomes. It is transparent enough that others have replicated and stress-tested it in many countries and datasets. Roughly a decade of scrutiny has refined magnitudes and exposed inference problems in shift-share designs, but it has not overturned the central result that adjustment is slow, costly and geographically concentrated. That result also changed how economists and policymakers think about the distributional and political consequences of globalisation. On the common criteria, I weigh direct evidential grounding of a first-order question and clean attribution first, and maturity second. This candidate is strong on the first two and adequate, though not exceptional, on maturity. I answer the chair's single-part question this way: I would not combine B044 with a one-name part. Splitting Autor from Dorn and Hanson would misstate who did the work. Round 2 should therefore consider single-part configurations.
statement.case_against: The strongest case against my choice is that B040 is older, more purely conceptual and more cleanly attributed to two originators. B044 rests on an empirical design and a body of findings, not a new framework. Its identification relies on shift-share instruments with known inference problems. The size, persistence and cause of the effects (trade versus automation) are still contested. The trade-shock papers date from about 2013, so long-run persistence is still being assessed, and several colleagues give recency real weight. A narrow citation also leaves the task-based and skill-bias strands, Katz's work and the Acemoglu lineage, outside the prize. A committee could reasonably see B044 as one strand of a larger literature rather than a closed achievement. My own reservations about B040 are real but are not about quality. They concern indirect empirical validation and the 2022 prize. They could be answered, so I treat the B040 versus B044 choice as close. I do not regard it as settled against B040.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B040 first and considers B044 only as an alternative. He argues that the task-based and trade-shock strands are separable, that a three-name cap makes the Dorn decision costly, and that B040 is less exposed on maturity. He says empirical directness should not outrank conceptual generality.
responses.response: I agree the strands are separable. That is why I anchor the citation on trade-shock evidence alone, where Dorn is as central as Hanson, and why I would not claim the task framework. Your conceptual-generality criterion is legitimate and I do not dismiss it. As a macroeconomist, though, I would add a caution from general knowledge that I have not verified here. How much amplification the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism produces in calibrated quantitative models has been contested. A prize resting on influence over how a field models credit is therefore partly a prize for an idea whose quantitative importance is unsettled. The China-shock result has the opposite profile, a smaller conceptual claim with a more directly measured effect. I weigh that difference as roughly even, not as a decisive point for either side. I accept your point that maturity favours B040, and I would not resist it if the committee weighs maturity above direct evidence.

responses.point: Andersson ranks B040 first and moved B044 up from eighth in his own comments. He still sees a structural problem, namely that the task-based and trade-shock strands may be two contributions with credit split across names. He wants the committee to settle which strand it is crediting before it settles the names.
responses.response: That is the right order of questions and my configuration answers it. The citation credits the trade-shock and local-labour-market evidence and nothing broader, so the names follow from the joint authorship of the core papers. On this reading the task-model authors are not omitted from this prize. They belong to a different achievement that this prize does not claim. I accept that the choice makes the award empirical-design-centred. Your reservation on recency is fair, but I think a decade of cross-country replication answers it better than it would have a few years ago. I also respect your caveat that validation of the collateral-constraint mechanism is mixed, and I would ask B040 supporters to weigh it with the same strictness they apply to shift-share inference.

responses.point: Teorell moved from B017 to B044 and argues that the task framework and the trade-shock evidence share one question about how technology and trade shift labour demand. He thinks one citation can cover both, and he names B040 as an alternative because of its cleaner attribution.
responses.response: I welcome the move and agree on the attribution of the core papers, but I would not adopt his wider citation. If the prize is said to cover technology and tasks, it implicitly credits a lineage (Levy-Murnane, Katz, Acemoglu, who is already a laureate) that Autor, Dorn and Hanson do not own jointly. The shared question is real, but a shared question is not a single achievement. The narrower wording is weaker on breadth but defensible on credit. I would accept the wider framing only if the committee shows that the task framework is itself part of what the three credited names established.

responses.point: Dreber-Almenberg ranks B040 first. She argues that the clean two-person attribution and nearly thirty years of use outweigh the thinner empirical validation. She suggests drafting the citation around the mechanism and its influence, not around confirmed magnitudes. She also says excluding Gertler and Gilchrist favours theory over tested evidence and that the committee should state this openly.
responses.response: I think her drafting proposal is the honest way to write a B040 citation, and it reduces my concern about indirect validation. A citation on the mechanism makes no empirical claim that the quantitative literature has not earned. It also shows what the committee would be choosing: a prize for a conceptual idea with some empirical support missing, not a prize for a tested one. For me that is a closer call than I wrote in round 1, and it is why B040 remains my first alternative. What still keeps B044 first for me is the combination of direct measurement and a first-order policy question. I hold it with moderate confidence. Her point on Gertler and Gilchrist is a fair statement of the cost of the two-name attribution, and I would not rest the exclusion on prior recognition.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B044 first and moved from Autor-Hanson to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. He anchors the citation on empirical evidence about trade and technology exposure and treats shift-share inference as refining rather than overturning the finding. He ranks B002 highly as an alternative but cites its shorter record.
responses.response: We agree on names and on the central point about inference. I would take one step further on the citation. 'Technology exposure' pulls the citation toward the task and automation debate, which is exactly where the effects are least settled, since part of the dispute is how much of the adjustment is trade and how much is automation. I would keep the wording to import competition so that the prize does not overclaim. On B002, we also agree. A Chetty-Hendren core would resolve my attribution concern, but long-run and external-validity evidence for place effects would need to accumulate before I move it from alternative to preferred.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges roughly a decade of replication enough maturity for B044 when B040 has nearly three decades of scrutiny, and whether I am underweighting that difference.
How large and persistent the China-shock effects are under alternative inference approaches for shift-share designs, and how much of the adjustment is trade rather than automation.
Whether an empirical design and a body of findings carries enough conceptual weight relative to a mechanism such as Kiyotaki-Moore, which is how B040 supporters see the choice.

How much the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises narrows B040, and how much the contested quantitative amplification in macro models narrows its claim. Both are based on members' knowledge and on mine, not on verification in this stage.
Whether the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity overlaps with B044 enough to weaken the marginal case. I currently judge the mechanisms and objects of identification to be different.

My position could change to B040 if colleagues show that its quantitative validation is stronger than I assume, or that B044's attribution is more fragile than I think. I have not changed it only to approach a majority, and I treat support counts as no evidence of merit.
statement.conflict_note: As secretary I am also a voting participant here by modeling assumption. No tie to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent in my supplied profile, and no credited name on B040 or B002 appears among my listed co-authors or institutional ties. My research on capital-skill complementarity and technological change is adjacent to the skill-bias literature behind B044, which could bias my weighting. I co-author with committee members Timo Boppart and John Hassler, and I am an IIES colleague of both; neither is a candidate, although Hassler supports B040 and Boppart supports B036. I also work in macroeconomics, the broad field of B040. I cannot verify from my profile whether any credited name on B017 has a connection to me, and B017 is not in my configuration or alternatives. All of this is disclosed and not adjudicated.
